## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sakabaḷa-sikkhāpada* constitutes the forty-third training rule (*sekhiya*) in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates monastic deportment and dining etiquette, setting down the precept against speaking while one's mouth is full of food (*na sakabaḷena mukhena giraṃ uccāressāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā*). Modern English translations of the rule include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

This rule belongs to a shared stratum of monastic etiquette found across Buddhist lineages. Curated parallels exist within the Pali tradition in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 43), the *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (Sekhiya 43), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Sekhiya 43), and the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*. Extensive cross-tradition parallels are preserved across Sanskrit manuscripts, Tibetan translations, and Chinese canonical versions, spanning the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinaya lineages.
